issues.legal_issue: Payments made to secure enduring protection benefiting a business as a whole are capital expenditure rather than deductible revenue expenditure.
material_facts: A company carrying on a manufacturing business paid recurring fees under lease covenants.
In return, the lessor undertook to restrict the grant of rights to other parties to extract limestone for cement manufacture in areas beyond the company’s leased quarries.
The protection benefited the company’s business as a whole for the duration of its lease, although one set of payments was made over a limited number of years.
The company claimed the payments as deductions in computing its business profits, and the tax authorities disallowed them as capital expenditure.
issues.conclusion: The payments secured an enduring advantage for the company’s business as a whole and were capital expenditure, not deductible under section 10(2)(xv) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922. The appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 10(2)(xv) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, only revenue expenditure is deductible. The court approved the broad principles stated in Benarsidas Jagannath, In re: expenditure is capital when its aim and object is to acquire an asset or enduring advantage for the business as a whole, rather than to run or work the business to produce profits. Whether a payment is recurring or made in instalments does not determine its character; the nature of what is acquired does. The fixed-capital and circulating-capital distinction may be considered where the enduring-advantage test does not resolve the matter. The court also relied on the enduring-benefit test in Atherton v. British Insulated and Helsby Cables Ltd. and the distinction between acquiring an income-earning asset and earning income discussed in Tata Hydro-Electric Agencies Ltd. v. Commissioner of Income-tax.

predicates.tax_deduction_appeal: A business challenges the disallowance of an expenditure deduction in a tax proceeding.
predicates.business_wide_enduring_advantage_acquire: The business paid for a lasting advantage that protected or improved the business as a whole.
predicates.operational_expense: The expenditure was incurred as part of the ongoing operations of the business to produce profits.

issues.definition: When a business challenges a disallowance and its expenditure acquired a lasting advantage for the business as a whole rather than being an operational expense, the expenditure is capital and is not deductible.
